title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
keyIdea: Recursion with processed (p) and unprocessed (up) strings: take the first digit of up, and for each of its letters recurse with p + letter and the rest of up. up empty → p is one combination. Each call returns its list; the caller concatenates.

approaches.name: Processed / unprocessed recursion
approaches.idea: gen(p, up): up empty → {p}; else for ch in mapping[up[0]]: add gen(p + ch, up.substr(1)) to the list.
approaches.why: Up to 4 letters per digit; each finished combination has length n.

quiz.q: What do p and up stand for?
options: p = letters chosen so far (processed), up = digits still left (unprocessed)

quiz.q: Why is there no undo step?
options: p + ch and up.substr(1) create new strings for each call

quiz.q: Why is it up to 4ⁿ and not 3ⁿ?
